prospect.name: Xiao Xie
prospect.aka: Roy — the rep addresses him as Roy throughout; the Zoom display label reads 'Xiao Xie - 295599'
prospect.location: Washington DC, USA — about a year; originally from Florida; considering a move to San Francisco
prospect.occupation: Full-time software engineer; building a language-learning app as a side venture (three days old at the time of the call, AI-assisted)
prospect.family_status: Partnered with a man for about 11 years; they plan a family via adoption in Asian countries or, failing that, surrogacy. Three nephews acquired in the last two years.
prospect.training_background: Overweight as a child, then lost it all in high school by 'How to Starve Myself'. Traditional barbell gym training for about ten years from age 19. Introduced to functional patterns three or four years ago by his partner. Found Trevor two or three weeks before the call and has been doing the free YouTube shorts workouts for about a week — currently 10 minutes three to four times a day because the sessions are intense. Previously 20-40 minutes four times a week. Also home calisthenics with a pull-up bar for a year, and a Caroline Girvan style dumbbell YouTube programme which injured his partner badly. Diets tried: carnivore/honey-fruit-and-meat, near-zero-carb, and meticulous calorie counting.
prospect.medical: Scoliosis, disclosed unprompted — 'I do have a scoliosis that I would love to, like, I don't know if that impacts it at all' — described as his upper body leaning one way. Audible cracking in the shoulders on movement, with limited shoulder range on one side. States no pain associated with either. Cannot touch his toes with straight legs; can hold a deep squat. Otherwise reports no health conditions. Sleeps well, needs about eight and a half hours.

signals: Already lean and training — 141 lb at a self-measured 12.9-13.1% body fat, four sessions a week — and explicitly chasing the last increment; the rep framed it accurately as 'we're looking at just how do we get that last stubborn couple percent'.
Successful and self-directed: full-time software engineer, building a second venture, has previously bought big-ticket coaching.
Goal is a system rather than a rescue: 'a sustainable place where I guess I do the steps and things just happen'.

DIVERGENCE: the optimizer is defined as treating price as a quality signal rather than a barrier, and here price was the entire blocker — not on affordability, which he confirmed ('we have the means to invest in this in cash'), but on a self-imposed rule about which money may be spent on what.

OVERLAP WITH skeptical_bargain_hunter: he is self-directed and capable, and the alternative he is anchored to genuinely works — a week of Trevor's free YouTube shorts already produced visible change, 'the fourth [ab] has been more defined than I could say it has ever been'. He was assigned optimizer on profile rather than bargain_hunter because he never argued the free version was sufficient and never contested the price as too high.

goals.text: Visible abs with minimal squeezable abdominal and back fat
A body he is proud of, tied directly to self-image and how he shows up
Nutrition and training on autopilot so it stops being daily crisis management — 'I just show up at the scheduled time and that's all I need to do'
Stop fitness being a background distraction while he builds a company
Show up self-assured in a new city and new professional rooms — 'the type of person to like walk up to someone random and introduce themselves'
Be a dad and husband his future family can say they are proud of
Improve shoulder and hip mobility, and endurance

pains.text: Daily guesswork — 'I'll wake up and it's kind of like crisis management sometimes... I don't know what to do for lunch, dinner, and what do I do for my workout?'
Eating oscillates between too little and too much with mixed results day to day
Childhood obesity that shaped his relationship with food, then losing the weight only by starving himself
Reached his happiest body at 134 lb but had no system to hold it
Burned by an expensive YouTube coaching programme where the work never seemed to hit the mark and momentum died
Scoliosis and shoulder restriction he is unsure about — 'I don't know if that impacts it at all'
Self-consciousness he expects to limit him socially and professionally in a new city
Would feel a vacation was wasted without something to show at the beach
Turning 30 and wanting this settled before then
Guilt about spending salaried income on himself, measured against a partner he describes as much more responsible with money

objections.raw_quote: the reason I'm hesitating is I've invested in, like, not in fitness, but in... Other types of coaching where it was a huge investment and I was disappointed and so that's I just want to be fully transparent about that
objections.rep_response: Normalised it with his own history — 'in the last eight years, I did the math. I think I spent over a couple hundred thousand dollars on like different coaches and mentorship... probably a solid 50 grand was like, dude, that probably wasn't worth it' — reframed the previous failure as a commitment problem rather than a product problem, then later offered the eight-kilogram guarantee as the answer.

objections.raw_quote: I think I might just, I might have to just think about it a little longer. If that makes sense.
objections.rep_response: Did not accept it. Re-ran the belief question, asked why, isolated the concern, then presented the price and continued closing for a further twenty-three minutes.

objections.raw_quote: it's more of a principle thing and not, like, I would have the means to invest in the course, it's just, like, do I feel like I deserve this course, you know?
objections.rep_response: Asked him to elaborate, then reframed the purchase from a splurge into an investment that funds the outcome he actually wants: 'what would happen if we looked at something like this, not as a splurge, but as an actual investment to help you get to the not-hard money?'

objections.raw_quote: It's something that I can delay for two to three months so that the transaction feels like aligned with my values.
objections.rep_response: Tested the premise — 'what happens as a hypothetical... if it doesn't take off within a couple of months?' and 'what happens if that one doesn't go through?' — then told a personal story about repeatedly deferring important things until finances improved and regretting it.

objections.raw_quote: The salary that we have as software developers, that's what we consider difficult money. Versus if we were to create an app that has passive income, that is considered not difficult money. And so I don't want to spend difficult money on this right now
objections.rep_response: Engaged it directly and inverted it — 'the purpose of earning the hard money is that so you can invest time, effort, and energy into getting the... easy' — getting the prospect to agree the hard money exists to fund the path to the not-hard money.

objections.raw_quote: I feel like my partner doesn't, it's like, much more responsible with money. But like, I just don't want to, like, I don't know, this is not a, like, must have thing.
objections.rep_response: The rep named the dynamic himself — 'then now I have to go to my partner, and he's really good with money, and I just be like, hey, I spent another X amount of dollars on it, and it didn't get me to what I wanted to' — the prospect confirmed it, and the rep then folded it back into the burned-before concern and never returned to it.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Improvised at 01:29:03 as a two-part package: a $1,200 first month under a 'love it or leave it' arrangement with no commitment beyond that month, and then 'we can probably just split up the payments remaining, where it's done on like a monthly basis, while you're in.' No number of instalments, no monthly figure, no total and no interest were stated. The rep said it required case-by-case sign-off: 'I have to get confirmation from Trevor on every time we do that.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'His guarantee is that you'll add at least eight kilograms to some of the main lifts... If for some reason we don't get you at least the eight kilograms, he's going to continue working with you for free until we're really dialed in.' Later restated as contractual and conditional: 'we'll increase your, your main list by eight kilograms when we put that in writing, where if you don't hit that, we'll continue working for you for free... Now that's predicated off you putting in the inputs, right?'

prospect_financials.note: He confirmed capacity without giving a figure — 'we have the means to invest in this in cash' — and estimated 'maybe a 1k surplus each month'. Asked directly for savings and checking balances he declined to give numbers. Credit cards, available credit and investments were never asked about.

evidence: No agreement and no payment. Asked whether the improvised structure would get him to commit, he answered 'That does, that does seem less of a painful decision to make' and then 'I'd have to check in on that.'

The rep tested for remaining hesitation and got it: 'I do sense there's a bit of hesitation still. Correct me if I'm wrong.' 'Yeah. I guess it's just like my, my, like my other obligations are also on my head.'

He gave a specific and repeated deferral horizon rather than a refusal: 'It's something that I can delay for two to three months' and 'next month would be, like, I am very interested in this program.'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: no follow-up call was booked, no link was sent and no next action was agreed. The rep closed it out with 'you know where to contact us if you ever switch up your mind', which is a rep treating it as dead rather than as a live follow-up.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the prospect never said no. Every value question came back positive — 'I definitely think I would get those results', 'I do' to whether it would be worth $6,000 — so it is scored follow_up rather than lost on the vocabulary as written.
The close ran through a disclosed hard stop; the prospect had a 5:30 commitment and was messaging someone during the last twenty minutes.
outcome.next_step: None agreed. The prospect said he would revisit in two to three months, once his app generates revenue; the rep left it on the prospect to make contact.

notable.note: Three things for a manager. First, scoliosis was disclosed unprompted, with the prospect openly asking whether it mattered — 'I don't know if that impacts it at all' — and the entire follow-up was one question about pain, after which a loaded overhead kettlebell programme was presented and pushed for ninety minutes. Second, the rep told the prospect he could effectively get coaching for his partner without paying for it, and said out loud that he was not supposed to: 'Trevor's, like, I'm technically not supposed to tell you this... if he's kind of following along with you, and he runs into a roadblock, just ask Trevor, he'll tell you.' Third, the objection was never about money. The prospect twice confirmed he could pay cash and that the outcome was worth $6,000; the blocker was a personal rule about spending salaried 'difficult money' on something with a soft return, compounded by an expensive coaching programme that burned him. The rep engaged that well and off-script, then closed with a $1,200 one-month trial and an unspecified instalment plan invented in the last two minutes of a ninety-minute call, against a hard stop.
